summary: Navajo Reservation lookout in San Juan County, NM; NHLR gives a 1936 build and an 82.9 ft International Derrick tower with a 7x7 cab; FFLA lists it standing.

facts.design: International Derrick tower with 7x7 metal cab (NHLR description)

events.note: Built in 1936 with a 7x7 metal cab, per the NHLR description and Built field
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on July 20, 2002 as US 434, NM 9

evidence.supports: Location in San Juan County, New Mexico
Administered by the Navajo Indian Reservation
Built in 1936 with a 7x7 cab; 82.9 ft high; on the Navajo Reservation
evidence.quote: One of these is Tohnitsha Lookout on the Navajo Reservation it is 82.9’ high with a 7’x7’ metal cab built in 1936.

evidence.supports: Register describes International Derrick towers of the 1930s and early 1940s; Aermotor is the most common design
evidence.quote: Although the Aermotor tower is most common, there were a number of International Derrick manufactured fire towers erected in the southwest in the 1930’s and early 1940’s.

evidence.supports: Listed as a standing tower with NHLR US 434, NM 9
evidence.quote: San Juan Tohnitsha 36.15392 -108.88982 Tower Standing NHLR US 434, NM 9

notes_for_editor: Only the NHLR entry and the FFLA New Mexico list give usable facts; no history, staffing, fire or fate record was found, so the story is thin. Brief record says access 'permission' and that Tohnitsha and Washington Pass share a register number; neither is supported: no fetched page states an access rule, and both sites give US 434 for Tohnitsha and US 435 for Washington Pass. Access left out of facts. Leads not cited (search snippet only, not fetched): a firelookout.org New Mexico table row seems to list International Derrick, 1936 and 82.6 ft; worth fetching to check the 82.6 vs 82.9 ft gap. The Forest Lookouts Weebly page for Tohnitsha holds only navigation text.
